calibration_rulings.title: Titles named after a person or a family (Al-Moosa, Al-Khalifa, Abdulrazaq Al-Arab): ruling N85's compound, or N101's possessive?
calibration_rulings.binds: musa-park::title, khalifa-museum::title and body, abdulrazaq-museum::title. Every later place named after a person (N85) and every later private museum named after its founder or his family (this item).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A FOR A PLACE NAMED IN HONOUR OF A PERSON OR FAMILY, B FOR A PRIVATE MUSEUM NAMED AFTER ITS FOUNDER OR HIS FAMILY. (1) musa-park keeps ruling N85's compound with no possessive, «الموسیٰ تفریح گاہ»: a public park whose possessive would say an ownership the sources do not state (the hospital co-founded the initiative); the reader passed it. (2) A private museum named after its founder or his family takes the Urdu possessive: «الخلیفہ کا ورثہ عجائب گھر», «عبد الرزاق العرب کا عجائب گھر». Ruling N85 is not reopened: its reason is that a possessive after a person's name 'says ownership', and for a private museum the ownership is what the sources say (the founder began it in his own garden and built the collection; the English body of abdulrazaq-museum says 'the museum of'). Ruling N101 (a place name + possessive) is untouched and gives «الاحساء کا عجائب گھر». THE TEST stage 4 named was the blind reader, and he failed the compound on both museums: «العرب» read as 'the Arabs' until the body's possessive (item 28, moderate), and «ورثہ» stuck between name and generic (item 32, his wording taken). Gender by the generic: musa-park's title feminine («تفریح گاہ»), the two museum titles masculine («عجائب گھر»). ROUND 2: CONFIRMED with its cost. The second reader read «الخلیفہ» as 'the Caliph's' and «العرب» as 'the Arabs' in the possessive titles, as the first had read «العرب» in the compound: the homograph belongs to the family name in any form and nothing inside the rulings fences it (no vowel sign, P8/P17; no word that says 'family', which no field states). The possessive is kept: it is the English body's own form for abdulrazaq-museum, and the first reader said it was what let him read a family name. Recorded for the owner. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; the list for the owner names no entry, and its decision 7 is the question this ruling concerns; it is entered with its open question stated, as b6 entered N93, N94 and N99 and b7 entered N106 and N110). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 7): The family names «الخلیفہ» and «العرب» read as "the Caliph" and "the Arabs" by both readers in both title forms; nothing inside the rulings fences them. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14), proof pass on round 2, note 6, record only (no string moves): the candidate list of this entry in the judge file, which the termbase does not carry, labels candidate A (the compounds, as the proof pass names them) "(in the text)", but the two museum compounds it quotes, «الخلیفہ ورثہ عجائب گھر» and «عبد الرزاق العرب عجائب گھر», are withdrawn and no longer stand in the text (musa-park's compound stays, as item (1) of the ruling says); the label reads "(stage 4's text)", the smallest correction the proof pass words. The ruling above says what replaced it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no possessive between a person's or family's name and the generic in the title of a place named in their honour (N85); a private museum named after its founder or his family carries «کا» after the name; the title key and every body mention of the page's name agree byte for byte.

calibration_rulings.title: The loan «اسٹیڈیم» (P16 / P16-test).
calibration_rulings.binds: stadium-park::title, summary, body. Every later page that names a stadium.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the loan «اسٹیڈیم» stands, masculine, plural unchanged; title «کھیلوں کے اسٹیڈیم کی تفریح گاہ», summary and body «کھیلوں کے اسٹیڈیم کے پہلو میں». Ruling P16 admits a loan with a dictionary entry where no common Urdu word exists in that meaning: the headword page (rekhta, HTTP 200 at stage 4) calls the loan itself the commoner form and defines a building with tiered seats, while «کھیل کا میدان» names a ground or pitch; the reference titles every stadium with the loan. The same case as «اسٹیشن» in ruling N106 (point 3). The blind reader read 'sports stadium' without a stumble. Entry verified (headword). B is refused: a stadium is not an open ground.
calibration_rulings.guard: Proofreader item 9: «اسٹیڈیم» is an admitted loan (its entry cites P16); «میدان» for a stadium is reported.

calibration_rulings.title: Two loans in the hospital's name.
calibration_rulings.binds: musa-park::body. Every later name of a hospital; «اسپیشلسٹ» as a common noun is not admitted.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «الموسیٰ اسپیشلسٹ ہسپتال». (a) «ہسپتال» is admitted under P16 as the common word: its headword is «اسپتال» (rekhta, masculine), the dictionary writes «ہسپتال» in its own definition of the native «شفاخانہ», and the reference has 3853 pages against 86 for the native word; entry verified, spelling of the reference. (b) «اسپیشلسٹ» stands INSIDE THIS INSTITUTION'S NAME ONLY, as Pakistani hospitals' names carry it; «تخصصی ہسپتال» is unattested (0) and reads as an Arabism; «خصوصی» changes the meaning. The reader passed the name. The name's entry stays pending (no Urdu page names this hospital).
calibration_rulings.guard: Proofreader item 9: «ہسپتال» is an admitted loan (entry cites P16); «اسپیشلسٹ» only inside the key «الموسیٰ اسپیشلسٹ ہسپتال».

calibration_rulings.title: khalifa-museum: village or town; and the area line's bare names.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, both questions. (1) Body: «الشعبہ اور القرین گاؤں کے درمیان» — the English noun and the line's entry for «الشعبہ» (a village), one generic after the list (ruling N76); village vs town classifies the same two places and changes nothing a visitor does; the Arabic's 'towns' logged. (2) Area line, raised under ruling N73's fence and ruled here by this page's judge: both names stay bare as both sources of the field have them; neither is a homograph of a common Urdu word, so N73's ground for completing does not arise. Source order (N30).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader: N76 (one generic after the list); a town or village named bare in both sources of an area line stays bare unless it is a homograph (N73).

calibration_rulings.title: ahsa-house-museum title.
calibration_rulings.binds: ahsa-house-museum::title and body. Not khalifa-museum::body, where «الاحساء کے گھر» is a topic in a list (see the ruling).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B: «الاحساء کے روایتی گھر کا عجائب گھر», masculine. The Arabic names a TYPE of house by an adjective Urdu may not coin (N115); «روایتی» restores the type, as the Russian title ('традиционного дома') and the Chinese '民居' do; the word is from another field and charged under accuracy (the model of N58). A is withdrawn on the reader (item 24, moderate: 'as if Al-Ahsa owned a house'); C («مکان») would still read as one house. The old key is retired. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED. The second reader found the title heavy (item 25, minor) but read it as a type of house: the first reader's moderate misreading is cured. SCOPE (proof on round 1, item 1): this item reaches the TITLE of ahsa-house-museum and its body mentions; the same Arabic phrase as a TOPIC in a list of sections (khalifa-museum: «الاحساء کے گھر، کھیتی باڑی، …… پر الگ حصے») stays «الاحساء کے گھر» — no reader stumbled on it there, and «روایتی» is not added where nothing needs it. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14), proof pass on round 2, note 6, record only (no string moves): the candidate list of this entry in the judge file, which the termbase does not carry, labels candidate A («الاحساء کے گھر کا عجائب گھر») "(in the text)", but that form is withdrawn and no longer stands in the text; the label reads "(stage 4's text)", the smallest correction the proof pass words. The ruling above says what replaced it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader: the title key byte for byte in title and body; no adjective of Al-Ahsa; «روایتی» is not required where the house is a topic in a list.
